raw_response:
I've been farming these 7 mu for 35 years now, since I was 18. My father taught me everything, and after all this time I mostly know what works and what doesn't. I'm 53 now, with my wife and my old mother at home, plus my son and his wife and their little one — six mouths to feed. My son helps when the factory in town gives him days off, but it's mostly me and my wife out there.

We do wheat-maize double cropping on all 7 mu. That's what my family has always done. Last year the wheat gave me about 400 kg per mu and the maize did about 450 kg. I'm hoping for about the same this year, maybe a little more if the rain cooperates.

For the wheat, I'll plant around October 10th, same as always. I buy improved seed from the county supply store — about 15 kg per mu, costs around 30 yuan. Before planting, I spread about 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu and work it in with the rotary tiller. That costs money, but if you skip the base fertilizer the wheat comes up yellow and weak. Then in March, at jointing, I watch the color. If it looks a bit pale, I topdress with about 15 kg of urea per mu. Some years I skip the topdress if the wheat looks green enough, but last year I put it on and the yield was good, so I'll probably do it again. I irrigate three times: once before winter to protect the seedlings, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. The electricity for the well pump isn't cheap, but three times is enough. I spray herbicide once in early spring. If I see aphids, I spray insecticide too — I lost half a mu to aphids about ten years ago and I don't let that happen again.

The maize goes in right after wheat harvest, around June 12th to 15th. The window is tight — sometimes we cut wheat in the morning and plant maize in the afternoon. I hire the combine for wheat harvest, costs about 50 yuan per mu, but it saves us two critical days. For maize I always buy fresh hybrid seed, about 3 kg per mu, costs around 45 yuan. You can't save maize seed, everyone knows that. I put all the fertilizer in at planting — about 40 kg of compound and 10 kg of urea per mu. There's no time for split application, the season is too short and I need to get it in fast before the soil dries. I irrigate twice for maize if it's dry, sometimes only once if the summer rains are good. I spray herbicide and usually insecticide once, because the corn borers always seem to come in August.

My wife and I do almost all the work. My son helps during wheat harvest and maize planting when it's frantic. I might hire one day of labor during the busy times if my son can't get off work, but I hate spending that money — 150 yuan a day now. On 7 mu you feel every yuan.

I figure my seed will cost about 525 yuan for both crops, fertilizer about 1,600 yuan, pesticides and irrigation another 700 or so, plus the combine hire. My total input costs this year should be around 3,300 yuan. That's a lot for me, but wheat and maize are steady. I don't take risks. Old Li down the road tried vegetables two years ago and lost money. I'll stick to grain.
